data.narrative:
Chaos Industries, a Series D–stage defense and security company that has raised over $1B cumulatively, is valued at $4.5B on a post-money basis. The relevant peer universe comprises three private Series D–stage comparables in the same sector (Helsing, Saronic, Onebrief) with valuations ranging from $2.1B to $18.0B, plus a broader ecosystem of ten public and private defense-tech peers including Anduril Industries and Shield AI.

Two valuation methods prove applicable. Stage-progression analysis, applying a typical 1.5x step-up multiplier from the last post-money valuation, yields $6.8B. Peer-median analysis across the three same-stage, same-sector comparables produces $9.2B, with the peer set exhibiting substantial dispersion (median $9.2B, range $2.1B–$18.0B). The peer-median approach captures material heterogeneity in the cohort—Helsing commands a 8.6x premium relative to Onebrief—reflecting differences in revenue scale, technology maturity, or customer concentration not isolated in this analysis.

Triangulating both methods produces a valuation range of $5.7B (low) to $10.6B (high), with a median point of $8.0B. This range sits materially above the current $4.5B valuation. Key uncertainties include revenue visibility, margin profile, and near-term funding requirements—data not provided here. The peer-median method carries higher weight given direct comparability, though the wide peer dispersion suggests sector-specific fundamentals warrant deeper diligence.
